sourceIssues.reason: 독수리 versus reference vulture/eagle taxonomy needs teacher/context review. Native draft uses vulture, matching explicit reference sense, without importing incorrect eagle claim.
Note omits the actual lexical Korean where word; source English description generalized. Translation retains description; no invented new form.
Source says casual speech only for close friends or younger people. Age alone is insufficient permission for casual speech; etiquette scope needs teacher review.
Only-daughter versus only-child terminology can depend on Korean dictionary usage; draft follows explicit reference only child (a daughter). Teacher must confirm intended concept.
Korean 형 encodes male speaker but English reference only says my older brother; native gloss keeps sibling relationship while original Korean remains authoritative for speaker evidence.
Korean 누나 encodes male speaker while English reference omits speaker gender; no inferred character setting added.
Classifier note describes after number and noun without explicit noun→number→classifier order. Native translation retains both dependencies; a teacher may clarify the ordering.
Double-batchim pronunciation rule is generalized and has lexical/phonological exceptions. Draft preserves source, not pronunciation-teacher approval.
ㅎ deletion rule is overbroad as a standalone statement; context pronunciation examples must be assessed by a teacher.
Present polite verbs do not all take an object; 을/를 applies to transitive constructions. Draft source rule retained, teacher scope review required.
